ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is parallelogram ABCD, vertex A is at the upper right, B is at the lower right, C is at the lower left, and D is on the left side; diagonal AC is drawn, and AC intersects another line segment at F. In the figure at point A, AC divides ∠DAB into two angles: ∠DAC is labeled 20°, and ∠CAB is labeled 32°. What is required is ∠BCD at point C. Then reason: Because ABCD is a parallelogram, AD ∥ BC and AB ∥ CD. Taking AC as a transversal, from AD ∥ BC we get ∠DAC = ∠BCA = 20°; from AB ∥ CD we get ∠CAB = ∠ACD = 32°. And ∠BCD is composed of ∠BCA and ∠ACD, so m∠BCD = 20° + 32° = 52°.
